_what_this_is: Reviewed-false-positive allowlist for the go-public scrub gate (oss_readiness.py). The scrub is a leak detector; because KRAKEN is a security tool, its own code legitimately handles the words token/password/secret and contains credential-detector marker strings, so the scrub trips on them. Every id below was individually reviewed on 2026-07-18 and confirmed non-sensitive. No real secret, endpoint, credential, or private-project linkage ships.
_reviewed: cve-reference: auto_cve_ingest.py and auto_patch_diff_score.py name public CVE IDs -- that is their function (a CVE-ingestion / patch-diff scoring helper). CVE IDs are public information, not sensitive.

license-conflict: auto_solidity_exploit.py emits GENERATED Solidity contract templates (Python functions returning Solidity source), and each carries the standard Solidity compiler SPDX MIT header. Solidity requires that header on generated output; it is the compiler convention for those templates, not a license claim on KRAKEN's own code, and does not conflict with the repo license.

secret / secret-in-history: src/kraken/helpers/auto_memory_dump.py contains the PEM key-header MARKER STRINGS a memory-dump credential detector searches FOR (standard OpenSSL/RSA/EC begin-markers) -- not embedded keys. The history scan re-flags the same strings from the committed blob. test fixture in tests/unit/tools/test_firmware_tools.py writes a placeholder key-shaped string to test the cred scanner.

secret-assignment: CTF/pwn-tool code that legitimately handles token/password/secret/api_key as its function (CTFd API client token params, JWT/hash crackers, exploit PoC generators, GraphQL payloads) plus test fixtures with obviously-fake values.
stub: flag-format placeholder strings (flag{test}, flag{TODO}, csawctf{) inside the solver's OWN flag-pattern regexes and wordlists -- not unfinished code.
